title: PROMOTION OF YOGA AND NATUROPATHY IN PUBLIC HEALTH
body_text:
Ministry of Ayush implements the Information Education and Communication (IEC) scheme to promote and propagate Ayush systems of medicine by conducting various awareness activities and programs for wider public outreach. Under this scheme, Ministry organises National/State level Arogya Fairs representing all system of Ayush including Yoga and Naturopathy, conducts Yoga Fests/ Utsavs and celebrates important days of Ayush system including International Day of Yoga which is celebrated on 21 st June annually. Further, Naturopathy Day is celebrated on 18 th November annually to create awareness about the principles and practices of Naturopathy and its role in promoting healthy lifestyle and wellness. The details of national programmes to promote Yoga and Naturopathy along with its expenditure is attached at Annexure I. The beneficiaries covered under these events are not limited to physical participation only as it engages beneficiaries through both physical participation and digital outreach on various social media platforms, thereby ensuring wider public outreach.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Ayush runs an Information, Education and Communication (IEC) scheme to promote Ayush systems, including Yoga and Naturopathy, through Arogya Fairs, Yoga Fests/Utsavs, International Day of Yoga (21 June) and Naturopathy Day (18 November). In a written reply in Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, shared expenditure details for these programmes from 2023-24 to 2025-26, showing a sharp rise in spending on International Day of Yoga from ₹24.16 crore to ₹57.38 crore. The outreach combines physical participation with digital engagement via social media platforms.
enrichment.context:
The Ministry of Ayush (Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy) was carved out as a separate ministry in 2014 to give focused attention to traditional and alternative systems of medicine and integrate them into India's public health strategy. The International Day of Yoga, observed on 21 June since 2015 following India's initiative at the UN General Assembly (which received record co-sponsorship), has become a flagship global soft-power and public health event, reflected in the ministry's rising expenditure on it. Naturopathy Day, observed on 18 November, commemorates Mahatma Gandhi's principles of nature cure and aims to popularize drugless therapies for lifestyle disease management, which is increasingly relevant given India's rising burden of non-communicable diseases.

These IEC activities align with the government's broader push for preventive healthcare, wellness tourism, and traditional medicine systems under initiatives like the National Ayush Mission, Ayushman Bharat's wellness centres, and India's leadership in establishing the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in Gujarat. Parliamentary questions and written replies of this nature are routine mechanisms for legislative oversight, ensuring transparency on how public funds are spent on health promotion schemes, and often serve as source material for current-affairs based UPSC questions on government schemes, health policy, and India's role in promoting traditional medicine internationally.

prelims_questions.question: International Day of Yoga is observed annually on which date?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that International Day of Yoga is celebrated on 21st June annually, following its adoption by the UN General Assembly at India's initiative.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is implemented by the Ministry of Ayush to promote awareness of Ayush systems including Yoga and Naturopathy?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that the Ministry of Ayush implements the IEC scheme to promote and propagate Ayush systems of medicine through awareness activities like Arogya Fairs and Yoga Fests.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of traditional systems of medicine like Yoga and Naturopathy in India's public health strategy. How can government schemes better integrate these systems into mainstream healthcare delivery?
India's promotion of Yoga through the International Day of Yoga has been described as an exercise in both public health outreach and soft power diplomacy. Critically examine this statement.
